description: ``patch FILE < diff`` applies an arbitrary diff to FILE — a write by any other name. The most common invocation form is ``patch -p1 FILE < diff`` where ``-p1`` glues the strip-level digit to the flag letter; flag-counting regexes that assume ``-X SPACE VAL`` miss this. Fix: capture the verb's full argument span and take EVERY positional plus a glued ``--output=``/``--directory=`` value (``_patch_targets``). NOT the last positional: ``patch [opts] [originalfile [patchfile]]`` WRITES its first positional and READS the last, so the ``_last_non_flag_token`` pick the other verbs share read ``patch <hook> p.diff`` as a write to ``p.diff`` and allowed it at every release before 2026-09-05 -- and every attempt below put the hook last, so the row never exercised the axis. The pick still handles ``patch FILE``, ``patch -p1 FILE``, ``patch -p 1 FILE``, ``patch --strip=1 FILE``, and ``patch -RpN FILE``.
